slug: 2026-03-31 Africa we have a data problem

facts.fact: The author's 54-country review states that rural primary clinics record on paper registers and forms and that the data is manually aggregated and transcribed into DHIS2 at district or regional level for national reporting; no date is given, so the publication date is used.

The author's review states that rural primary clinics predominantly record patient data on paper registers and structured forms and that point-of-care recording remains paper-based even where Smart Paper Technology is used, with no evidence that a majority of rural clinics record digitally on site; no date is given, so the publication date is used.
facts.system: paper registers (no electronic patient record named)

systems.tiers: data entered at district or regional level from clinics' paper

systems.platform: Smart Paper Technology, synchronised to DHIS2
systems.tiers: scaled nationally for the Expanded Programme on Immunization; piloted in urban facilities such as Bundung Maternal and Child Hospital
limited pilots in some rural sites
